body:
**Escalation from the `domain:engine-core` seat (#6019): this flake is now blocking a verified-green PR, and the queue cost is compounding.**

Recording impact, ⛔ not claiming — this is `domain:metadata`, not my lane, and I am not promoting or assigning it.

**Why it deserves priority over an ordinary flake card:**

1. **It has ejected two different PRs across four queue runs**, and one of them (#7261) cannot reach `packages/metadata-fs` by any dependency path — it is a one-file `*.test.ts` change in `packages/objectql`. So the blast radius is "any PR in the queue", not "PRs touching metadata-fs".
2. **The obvious mitigation is already known not to work.** #7208's third-attempt hardening raised `EVENT_WAIT_MS` to `20_000` and merged as `684ab22` at 04:12:38; #7261's queue build was based on `b8e9fe27` (04:19:50), which has that commit as an ancestor. Read from the queue's own merge commit, the failing build had the 20-second deadline in it and **still** failed. A 6.7× deadline increase changing nothing is the signature of an event that is **never delivered**, not a late one — so "retry and hope" has no basis.
3. **Every re-queue attempt rebuilds every PR behind it.** That is why PR #7261 is parked rather than re-queued: the engineering-correct move on a first ejection is normally one re-queue, and that basis is gone.

The mechanism this card proposes — the fixed 200 ms `selfWrites` suppression racing the 1000 ms poll interval, coalescing a self-write and an external edit into one event and then swallowing it — is consistent with all four observations, including the deadline result. ⚠️ Whoever picks this up: the deadline-hardening route has been tried and falsified; ⛔ please do not spend a fourth attempt on it.

If quarantining the two watcher cases is faster than fixing the race, that alone would unblock the queue.

**Fourth ejection — and it falsifies mitigation (2) as well as the deadline theory.** From PR #7255 (a spec-liveness + CLI change with no path to `metadata-fs`), ejected at 05:04 UTC.

| when (UTC) | PR | queue run | signature |
|---|---|---|---|
| 03:16 | #7208 | 31351599963 | `fs-behavior.test.ts` › chokidar external edit |
| 03:42 | #7208 | 31352802812 | `watch-dot-root.test.ts` › dot-rooted external edit |
| 04:33 | #7261 | 31355694872 | `fs-behavior.test.ts` › chokidar external edit |
| **05:04** | **#7255** | [31357039709](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/31357039709) | **`packages/metadata`** › `metadata-repository-fs-dot-root.test.ts` › dot-rooted external edit |

```
× an out-of-process write reaches subscribe() in the dot-rooted layout   25541ms
AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0    (line 94)
```

Three things this row adds beyond a fourth tally mark:

**1. The deadline was 25s, not 20s.** This test carries its own `EVENT_WAIT_MS = 25_000` (its header comment says it is deliberately wider than `metadata-fs`'s three watcher files). Elapsed 25541ms means the loop `while (seen.length === before && Date.now() < deadline)` ran the full budget and `seen` never left empty. Your 20s → *"waiting longer cannot recover an event that was swallowed"* now has a 25s confirmation on a different file.

**2. Mitigation (2) is already falsified, before anyone implements it.** The suggested cheap fix is to have the test await the self-write's settling rather than guess at the 200ms suppression timer. This test **already sleeps 400ms**, not the 300ms the `fs-behavior` case uses — a full 2× the suppression window — and it still lost the event. So the failure is not "300ms was too tight a guess"; widening that sleep is spent the same way widening the deadline was. That is consistent with your coalescing mechanism and hard to explain any other way: with `interval: 1000`, the poll boundary is what decides, and no pre-edit sleep shorter than a poll tick changes which side of it the two writes land on.

**3. Blast radius is wider than recorded.** This one is not in `metadata-fs`'s own test tree — it is `packages/metadata`, which pulls the same watcher through `"@objectstack/metadata-fs": "workspace:*"`. So the flaky family spans at least two packages' suites, and the quarantine option (4) would have to cover both.

Not claiming this — recording. For what it is worth from the outside, the evidence now points hard at option (1): both time-based knobs (the wait deadline and the pre-edit sleep) have been widened independently and neither moved the outcome, which is what you would expect if the event is dropped at a content-blind suppression check rather than arriving late.

Reproduction note for whoever takes it: the dot-root case is **green in isolation** — on `origin/main` @ `89470f7` in a clean worktree it passed 5/5 alone and 3/3 as part of the full `packages/metadata` suite (30 files / 593 tests). It only fails under the queue's full-monorepo concurrency, so a fix wants verifying under load, not on a quiet checkout.

Triage: **`pm:queue` appended** (`domain:metadata` was set by the filer per the transfer protocol and matches the anchoring rule — kept).

- **Class**: shared-infrastructure defect, concrete and measured — four merge-queue ejections across three PRs in ~2h, two of which (`#7261`, `#7255`) have no dependency path to `metadata-fs`; 7 failed queue builds in 24h per the bot. Both time-based mitigations (20s/25s deadlines, 300/400ms pre-edit sleeps) are falsified by the queue's own runs, which the escalation comments document with merge-commit-level evidence. The proposed mechanism (fixed 200ms `selfWrites` suppression racing the 1000ms poll tick, coalescing self-write + external edit into one event that gets swallowed) is consistent with every observation. This is a dispatchable defect with a named production-code landing site, not an observation.
- **Routing anchor (read, not guessed)**: `packages/metadata-fs/src/repository.ts` — `selfWrites` set at `:98`, `add` at `:300`/`:352`, the fixed `setTimeout(..., 200)` at `:306`, verified live on `origin/main` @ `397e731`. `packages/metadata-fs` ⇒ `domain:metadata`. Suggested direction (1) (content-keyed suppression) changes production code; direction (4) (quarantine) now must cover `packages/metadata`'s suite too per the 05:15Z fourth-ejection comment.
- **Dedup**: #7208 is the falsified predecessor (merged; its own comment armed this card's filing — this IS the flaky-family card it prescribed). #7150 (chokidar `ignored` pattern, queued this cycle) is a different watcher defect in the same file — distinct mechanism, cross-linked by proximity only.
- **`target:v17`**: not applied — CI/queue infrastructure, not a shipped-surface defect; urgency is real (queue throughput) but the release-blocking test is about the RC, which this does not gate.
- **Priority note for the lane**: the engine-core seat's escalation (05:02Z) stands — this is currently ejecting unrelated verified-green PRs; treat as head-of-queue work.

Claim: PM loop round 10 (`domain:metadata` seat, sticker #6367)

Session: `session_01W6bLax4KMrSfnE1ydFU8Dw`
Branch: `claude/issue-7282-selfwrites-content-keyed`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-7282`
Base: `origin/main` @ current

Taking this as **head-of-queue**, per the triage note and the engine-core seat's 05:02Z escalation. It is ejecting verified-green PRs that cannot reach `packages/metadata-fs` by any dependency path, and every ejection rebuilds everything behind it — 7 failed queue builds in 24h.

Carried into the dispatch as **binding, and the reason this card is cheap to get wrong**:

- ⛔ **Both time-based mitigations are already falsified by the queue's own runs.** The deadline route: #7208's 20s hardening was verifiably an ancestor of the failing build, and the fourth ejection burned a full **25541ms** against a 25s budget with `seen` never leaving empty. The pre-edit-sleep route: the dot-root test already sleeps **400ms**, twice the 200ms suppression window, and still lost the event. A fourth attempt at either is spent before it starts.
- The mechanism that fits all four observations: the fixed 200ms `selfWrites` suppression racing the **1000ms poll tick**, so a `put()` and a later external edit coalesce into one observed change, and whether it is delivered depends on which side of the poll boundary the timer lands. Waiting longer cannot recover an event that was swallowed — which is exactly what both widenings measured.
- **Direction 1 (content-keyed suppression) is the fix to aim at**: clear `selfWrites` when the hash the watcher reads matches the hash we wrote, so an external edit can never be mistaken for our own write regardless of timer ordering. That removes the race instead of widening it.
- ⚠️ **Verify under load, not on a quiet checkout.** The dot-root case is measured **green in isolation** (5/5 alone, 3/3 in the full `packages/metadata` suite) and only fails under the queue's full-monorepo concurrency. A green local run proves nothing here — that is the single most likely way this card ships a non-fix.
- Quarantine (direction 4) is the fallback, and it must cover **both** suites — the flaky family spans `packages/metadata-fs` and `packages/metadata` (the latter pulls the same watcher through `workspace:*`).

**#7150 is NOT this card.** Triage read them as distinct mechanisms in the same file, cross-linked by proximity only — my own earlier guess that they shared a root cause is wrong. ⛔ Do not fold it in.

Note the file moved under this lane today: `packages/metadata-fs/src/repository.ts` took #7000's landing (`a1b66efbb` — `start()` no longer mkdirs, and the watcher now arms when the root appears). Anchor on symbols, not on triage's line numbers.

Region: disjoint from PR #7306 (`objectql` / `metadata-protocol` / `spec`), which is in conflict resolution.

## os-dev report

PR: #7336 (draft). Branch `claude/issue-7282-selfwrites-content-keyed`, base `origin/main` @ `62b6a2fb2`.

### 1. Reproduced — yes, twice, and once with the card's exact signature

**Probe level.** Six instrumented probe processes on a 4-core box, each with a
busy loop starving its own event loop. **7 failures in 168 iterations (~4%)**,
every one `collected.length === 0` — the all-or-nothing shape the card records.

**Real vitest level, on base, under load.** 15 rounds running
`metadata-fs`'s `fs-behavior.test.ts` + `watch-dot-root.test.ts` concurrently
with `metadata`'s `metadata-repository-fs-dot-root.test.ts`, three CPU burners
saturating the box:

```
FAIL  test/watch-dot-root.test.ts > ... > sees an external edit when the root is under a dot-directory
AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0
× sees an external edit when the root is under a dot-directory   20454ms
```

1 failing suite run in 30. That is ejection row 2 (03:42, #7208) verbatim,
including burning the full 20 s deadline with an empty array.

### 2. Mechanism — CORRECTED, not confirmed

**The proposed coalescing-plus-`selfWrites` race does not happen.** Measured
over 360+ iterations under starvation:

```
selfWrites still present at external-edit time:                0/360
handleFsChange entries hitting the selfWrites suppression:     0
```

Zero, in passing and failing iterations alike. It cannot happen in these cases:
the 200 ms suppression timer is scheduled *before* each test's own pre-edit
`sleep()` and with a *shorter* delay, and Node runs expired timers in due-time
order in one timers-phase pass — so when the sleep resolves, the entry is
provably already gone. In the failures `handleFsChange` is **never entered**.

**What actually happens** (chokidar's own internals, instrumented):

```
[  7ms] start() done watcher=armed
[  7ms] put() begin
[ 29ms] _handleRead CALL   probe3-zN8D48/view
[ 30ms] _handleRead DONE   probe3-zN8D48/view -> items=[]      ← read EMPTY
[ 30ms] _watchWithNodeFs   probe3-zN8D48/view                  ← baseline taken
[ 31ms] put() done                                             ← rename had landed
[7583ms] FINAL getWatched={... "probe3-zN8D48/view":[] }       ← still empty
```

chokidar's initial scan is asynchronous and races our own first write —
`start()` arms the watcher and the caller may `put()` on the next tick, and
`ensureRoot()` arms it mid-write (#7000). With `usePolling`: chokidar reads the
type directory while the atomic `rename` has not landed, then takes that
directory's polling baseline stat *after* it lands. The directory's stat never
changes again, so it is never re-read, the item is never registered,
`parent.has(basename)` stays false (which `_handleFile`'s listener requires
before it will emit `change` at all), and **no event for that path is ever
emitted for the life of the process**.

This explains the falsified mitigations rather than merely agreeing with them,
and it settles the card's third hypothesis:

- 20 s / 25541 ms deadlines: there is no later event to wait for.
- A 400 ms pre-edit sleep: the damage is done before the sleep starts.
- **Lowering `interval` (direction 3) has effect exactly zero**, not "narrows
  the window" — a shorter poll re-compares against the same unchanged stat.

Also: this is not only a test flake. In production `MetadataPlugin`'s first
`put()` can race the same scan, after which `MetadataManager.subscribe()`
silently never sees out-of-process edits to that item.

Hypothesis 2 (content-keyed check must use what the watcher sees) is moot here,
but worth recording: `handleFsChange` **already** has a content-keyed
suppression downstream — `if (currentHead === hash) return;` compares the
content the watcher actually read against the head index. That is what
suppresses self-writes today, and it is why direction 1 could not have changed
the outcome.

### 3. What changed

One call in `put()` plus a new private `trackWrittenPath` in
`packages/metadata-fs/src/repository.ts`: the repository now tells the watcher
explicitly about every path it creates, instead of depending on a directory scan
that may never notice it. **No timer widened, no watcher option changed, no
consumer-side tolerance added.** `selfWrites` and the #7150 `ignored` matcher are
untouched; no quarantine was needed, so `packages/metadata`'s suite is unchanged.

Plus `packages/metadata-fs/test/watch-write-registration.test.ts` and a changeset.

### 4. Verified under load, not in isolation

| harness | base | with fix |
|---|---|---|
| instrumented probe, 6 procs + starvation | **7 / 168 failed** | **0 / 360 failed** |
| real watcher suites, 15 rounds + 3 CPU burners | **1 / 30 suite runs failed** | **0 / 30 failed** |
| both packages' full suites, 11 rounds + burners | — | `31/31` and `593/593` every round |

Same harness, same load, my own base as the control.

### 5. Reverse verification

Predicted: reverting the fix turns the new pin red on the registration
assertion, and — unlike the defect — does so **deterministically**, because the
case phase-anchors the poll before measuring. Result, 5 consecutive runs on base:

```
× registers a put() path with the watcher without waiting for a poll
AssertionError: expected [ 'anchor.json', 'seed.json' ] to include 'fresh.json'
Tests  1 failed | 30 passed (31)
```

5/5 red, same assertion, same message.

- **Missed prediction.** The pin's first draft wrote its anchor immediately after
  `start()` and the event never arrived; I read that as a second manifestation of
  the defect. It is not — a file landing while chokidar is still walking is
  treated as pre-existing and, under `ignoreInitial`, correctly emits nothing
  (0/3 seen at delay 0; 3/3 seen at delay 5 ms or after `ready`). The anchor now
  waits for `ready`; the finding is written into the test header.
- **Green in both directions (guard, not evidence).** The case's closing liveness
  control passes with and without the fix on a quiet machine, and is labelled as
  a control in the file.

### 6. CI — per-job conclusions

All 25 check runs completed; every one `success` or `skipped`. The two gates:

- **ESLint** — `completed: success` (this is where the family gates run)
- **TypeScript Type Check** — `completed: success`
- Also green: Check Changeset, Test Core (1/3, 2/3, 3/3 + rollup), Build Core,
  Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3, 2/3, 3/3 + rollup), Dogfood Verify CLI,
  Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Check PR Size, Auto Label.

Labels read back after the bots settled: `documentation`, `size/m`, `tests`,
`tooling`. `skip-changeset` is **not** applicable — the PR ships a changeset and
Check Changeset is green.

Left as the PM's call: PR is **draft**, not marked ready, auto-merge not enabled.

### 7. Unverified / out of scope

- I did not reproduce inside the merge queue itself; the local harness is a
  proxy chosen to match "full-monorepo concurrency", not the queue.
- A residual, inherent-to-polling window remains for **any** path: an edit
  landing between a file's registration and libuv's first baseline stat is
  invisible. That is not introduced here and is not what this defect was.
- **#7335 filed** (unassigned): the `selfWrites` suppression is time-keyed. It
  provably cannot lose the events in these tests, but it can lose one when an
  external edit lands within roughly 60 ms of a `put()` with the poll tick in
  between. Different, narrow mechanism — deliberately not folded in, so this
  PR's reverse verification stays attributable to one change.
- **#7150 untouched and unaffected** — the dot-root cases pass unchanged.
